intro.title:
Copy a value,
then change it
intro.subtitle: Does the copy change too?
intro.note: One small C example. Two integer variables.
intro.vo: If we copy a number into another variable, will both change together? Let us trace one small example in C.

scenes.title: Start with x equal to ten
scenes.subtitle: Read one instruction at a time.
scenes.vo: First, we create an integer variable named x. Its value is ten. Keep this value in view as we add a second variable.

scenes.title: Copy the current value
scenes.subtitle: Assignment reads x and stores that value in y.
scenes.vo: Next, we create y. We copy the value from x into y. Both now contain ten. This assignment copies a number; it does not link the two variables together.

scenes.title: Change x and check y
scenes.subtitle: Two variables retain their own values.
scenes.vo: Now we change x to twenty. Watch the new number arrive in x. The value in y remains ten, because y received a copy earlier. Changing x does not repeat that assignment.

outro.title:
Two variables,
two values
outro.subtitle: Assignment copies the value at that moment.
outro.note: This example uses ordinary integers, not pointers or shared objects.
outro.vo: An integer assignment copies the current value. Afterwards, these two variables hold their own numbers. To change y, we need another assignment to y.
